compute_serverless.rationale: Pure event-driven serverless compute (Lambda, App Runner) is billed per invocation; deployments in the DR region cost nothing until traffic arrives. Note: Lambda Provisioned Concurrency is available for warm-capacity scenarios that need pre-warmed runtimes; if used in DR, that line item will appear in the bill and be priced directly.

compute_server.rationale: Server-shaped or task-shaped compute (EC2, ECS/EKS Fargate, Batch, Beanstalk) runs no DR-region capacity at backup-restore or pilot-light. Warm standby runs ~50% of primary capacity per AWS Well-Architected guidance, with Auto Scaling configured to ramp to 100% on failover. Active/active runs full capacity in each Region so either can absorb the other's load with no ramp, roughly doubling total compute.

data.rationale: Data services replicate continuously across DR postures. Backup restore = snapshot-only; pilot light = small standing replica or storage-only replication; warm standby = scaled-down full replica running at the DR region; active/active = full mirror with replication overhead.

networking.rationale: DR-region load balancers, NAT gateways, VPC endpoints, and similar networking surface are pre-deployed at pilot-light for fast cutover and run at ~50% of primary surface for warm standby and active/active. Edge-only services like Route 53 and CloudFront resolve at curated entries first and may overshoot the category default; their absolute cost is small enough that the difference is rounding.

streaming.rationale: Streaming services have provisioned capacity costs (shards, partitions) even without traffic.

management.rationale: Security and management services have small incremental costs for monitoring DR region resources.
